findings.message: Async OpenAI chat.completions.create() response is never inspected for .usage. Without reading response.usage (total_tokens, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens), you have no visibility into token consumption or API cost. Log usage after the await or instrument with a proxy like Helicone or Langfuse.

OpenAI API call without `seed` parameter. Without a fixed seed, prompt caching is unreliable and outputs are non-deterministic across identical inputs. Add `seed=42` (or any fixed integer) to enable deterministic caching and reduce redundant API costs.

OpenAI client instantiated without a timeout. Without a timeout, API requests can hang indefinitely — the model runs (and you are billed) while your process blocks. Set timeout=30.0 (seconds) or use httpx.Timeout for fine-grained control. In agent loops, a single hung request can block all downstream tasks.

OpenAI Responses API call is missing max_output_tokens or max_completion_tokens. Without this cap, models like o3 may generate extremely long responses at high cost. Add max_output_tokens=<limit> or max_completion_tokens=<limit> to all responses.create() calls.

Consolidate retrieval + generation into a single prompt, or use structured tool-calling to avoid redundant model invocations.
